statuses.proven: Engine-level byte-grounded proof exists (VM golden and/or CFG trace against the real retail disassembly), matching this project's other natural-route rigor. Live in-browser wiring is NOT required for this status -- several proven legs in this corpus (e.g. Secret's and CoK's own quest legs) are engine-proven only, by explicit, documented precedent (Secret's Sixth Route, CoK's Sixth Route). Counts as PASSING the campaign gate.
statuses.structurally-absent: Investigated and found to genuinely not exist in the game's own retail content (e.g. no WILDCOM.DAX shipped, zero relevant opcode writes anywhere in the ECL corpus) -- a proven negative, not an unresolved gap. Counts as PASSING the campaign gate.
statuses.blocked: Investigated with genuine effort and found genuinely unresolved or structurally unreachable with the game's own real content (e.g. a bounded cross-block quest scan found no genuine producer-to-consumer link). Different in kind from structurally-absent: this is "we looked, it's blocked," not "we looked, it's proven not there." Counts as FAILING the campaign gate.
statuses.not-tracked: Never part of this game's own BUILD-QUEUE matrix bullet scope (e.g. CoAB's own matrix bullet only ever listed 5 legs: early/middle/ending/town/wilderness -- quest was never separately tracked for CoAB). Counts as FAILING the campaign gate -- an untracked leg is not evidence of anything, positive or negative, so it cannot be treated as satisfied.
statuses.not-investigated: No dedicated investigation of this leg has been run for this game yet. Deliberately distinct from `blocked` (we looked and it is genuinely unresolved) and from `structurally-absent` (we looked and it provably does not exist in the retail content): this status asserts nothing about the leg except that the work has not been done. Counts as FAILING the campaign gate, for the same reason `not-tracked` does -- an uninvestigated leg is not evidence of anything.

TWO MEN WATCH, AND ONE OF THEM IS SAYING '...HIM TRY TO CAST A SPELL--THEY'LL TEAR HIS ARMS OFF!'"; post-victory "'WELL, WELL, WELL,' ... Registry seeded: `tools/map_gen1_cross_area_flag_reads.py` gained a `gateway-to-the-savage-frontier` FLAG_REGISTRY entry (additive only; the scan was run with explicit `--json`/`--markdown` into a session scratchpad, the checked-in corpus report was NOT touched).

(c) `[0x4BF2]=21` and `[0x03B2]=2` are host inputs that only select which of the block's own spawn arms runs; the fork itself is asserted independently of the spawn. (d) Cross-block memory continuity is modelled as one flat 16-bit-word Map, never natively observed; the retail scripts use [0x4C20]/[0x4C21]/[0x4C22] as independent adjacent flags, which implies byte-addressed storage — for 0/1 values the two models coincide and nothing here depends on the difference. (g) The Gateway dialect discriminates against `ECL_GEN1_SHORT` (which desyncs and loses the roster and COMBAT entirely) but NOT against plain long `ECL_GEN1`, which gives an identical result — so this route alone does not prove the Gateway split (test L). town.citation:
NWN-DOS `town` leg = PROVEN on `ECL0.DAX#1` / `GEO0.DAX#1` (Neverwinter). Doc `docs/engine/research/nwn-town-route.md`; golden `packages/engine/test/nwnTownRoute.test.ts` (14 tests, 14 pass, retail-byte-backed, not skipped when the install is present). Dialect ECL_GEN1 (long frame); vbase 0x7FFE, file_offset = vaddr-0x8000+2. Header of ECL0#1 (4808 b), re-read as `88 13` + five `01 01 <vaddr>` far pointers: vm_run_1 0x82FC, search_location 0x81E1, pre_camp_check 0x839A, camp_interrupted 0x83C5, initial_entry 0x8014 (= file offset 22).

DISCRIMINATOR. `inDungeon` [0x4BE6] is written ZERO times corpus-wide (confirmed by two independent methods), so no engine-mode signal exists; the town signal is the retail town-service dispatch — `SAVE #1,[0x7F6C]` EnterShop, `SAVE #1,[0x7EE2]` EnterTemple, `SAVE #127,[0x7EA8]` training_class_mask adjacent to COMBAT / PROGRAM #0. CORRECTION to the earlier framing: the conjunctions do no work. `EnterTemple` ALONE selects exactly {ECL0#1, ECL1#12, ECL2#24, ECL2#25} — identical to {EnterShop AND EnterTemple}; `training=127` ALONE selects exactly {ECL0#1, ECL2#25} — identical to the triple. The honest statement is that ONE flag, EnterTemple, is the whole discriminator, and its strength is that it has zero false positives over 33 blocks, not that a cluster narrows anything.

CENSUS over 6 ECL archives / 33 blocks, re-derived twice: EnterShop 20 sites / 13 blocks; EnterTemple 4 / 4; training_class_mask 33 sites (31 write 0, exactly 2 write 127 — ECL0#1@0x87D6, ECL2#25@0x96E7); game_area [0x7F12] 9 naive / 8 instruction-reachable (all 9 write the constant 1, so it shows the address is used, not what it means in NWN); inDungeon 0 by both methods. All four selected blocks are settlements: "WELCOME TO NEVERWINTER!" @0x815D, "'WELCOME TO TRIBOAR,' SAYS THE INNKEEPER. 'WOULD YOU LIKE TO REST FOR 1 PLATINUM?'" @0x89AA, "'WELCOME TO NIGHTSEDGE'" @0x936D; ECL2#24 is identified only INDIRECTLY, from a guard's line "…MORE DANGEROUS THAN HERE IN FLOODBLEST" @0x9135. Priced innkeeper rests exist in all four — ECL0#1@0x870D (1 pp), ECL1#12@0x89AA (1 pp), ECL2#25@0x8AAB (5 pp), ECL2#24@0x95EC (1 pp; NOT the sign at 0x8E03 the golden cites). Zero dungeon blocks selected.

STRUCTURE. `search_location` @0x81E1 masks the descriptor `AND #127,[0xC04F],[0x4C02]`, then `COMPARE [0xC04F],#129 / IF_LT / GOTO 0x827C` forks on bit 7 into a 38-arm DOORWAY `ON_GOTO` @0x8204 (file offset 518) and a 38-arm STREET-SIGN `ON_GOTO` @0x8284 (offset 646). Both open `25 01 02 4c 00 26` — the SAME selector [0x4C02] and the same fork — so their agreement is a consistency check on one shared index rendered twice, not two independent indices. Door arms: 3→0x869E weaponry, 4/5/6→0x8832 temple, 7→0x8404 general, 8→0x8462 silver, 9→0x84BA jeweller, 10/11/12/13→0x87A3 training, 15–36→0x831F EXIT, 37→0x92C2. Sign arms 5/6/7/8 all →0x8996 "ADVANCE LEVELS HERE". Cold boot: `initial_entry` @0x8014 compares [0x4BF2] against 51/127/1/2/3/4/27/28; a zero LastEclBlockId matches none and falls through to the default arm @0x8138 → x=8, y=7, facing=3 (west).

GEO0#1 is 1026 b, 16x16; descriptors raw[514+y*16+x] (engine `decodeGeoBlock` floor == that byte, 0/256 mismatches); spawn (8,7) is descriptor 0. Neverwinter has TWO shopping districts (west: doors x=6 / signs x=7, y=2..4; south-east: doors y=11 / signs y=10, x=13..15). GEOMETRY, stated in the direction golden test N actually asserts (SIGN→DOOR): every cell carrying sign descriptor 11/12/13/16/17/18/6/22 is orthogonally adjacent to exactly one door of the paired type — general 11 @(7,2),(14,10) ↔ doors 135 @(6,2),(14,11); silver 12 @(7,3),(13,10) ↔ 136 @(6,3),(13,11); jewelry 13 @(7,4),(15,10) ↔ 137 @(6,4),(15,11); temples 17/16/18 @(10,5),(10,9),(10,12) ↔ 133 @(10,4),(10,10),(10,13); training 6 @(7,11) ↔ 139 @(6,11); Cragdyk 22 @(12,6) ↔ 131 @(13,6). The DOOR→SIGN direction is NOT claimed and is not true: the training arm 0x87A3 is entered from descriptors 138/139/140/141 = eight cells (6,10)-(6,13) and (14,0)-(14,3), of which only (6,11) and (14,1) (sign 7 @(13,1), same 0x8996 arm) touch a sign cell at all; the weaponry descriptor 131 occupies four cells (8,0),(13,6),(15,8),(6,15), advertised by four different arms-&-armor signs — 9 KROEGEL'S @(8,1), 3 BAYLESS @(14,8), 1 BRORSMAN'S @(6,14), 22 CRAGDYK'S @(12,6). Arms cover more cells than the doc's per-building table lists: shops 8 door cells, temple 3, jeweller 2, training 8.

ROUTE. A 42-step circuit from (8,7) visits all six service doors. Re-measured off the raw GEO planes: 29 edges are wall slot 0 / door flag 0, and the remaining 13 all carry door flag 1 — no flag-2/flag-3 edge and no non-zero-wall-with-door-flag-0 edge anywhere — so every step is unconditional. Each cell was dispatched through the real `EclVm` from a FRESH memory map, i.e. 42 independent single-cell dispatches, not a continuous retail traversal.

LIMITS. NWN has NO Town engine mode — Neverwinter is mechanically an ordinary dungeon-mode stepped grid with shops on it. The mapping EnterShop/EnterTemple/training → `CityShop()`/`temple_shop()`/`startGameMenu()` and the Area2 address model `offset = (loc*2 + 0x800) & 0xFFFF` are inherited from the CoAB source oracle (`coab_extracted/Classes/Area2.cs` offsets 0x550/0x5C4/0x624/0x6D8/0x6DA/0x7EC; `engine/ovr003.cs CMD_Combat`; `engine/ovr008.cs vm_SetMemoryValue`; `Classes/Opperation.cs GetCmdValue`); NWN's own GAME.EXE/GAME.OVR was NOT disassembled — the single largest inference. Cross-title control: Gateway's proven town block ECL5#19 writes all three flags (raw-byte census 2/2/1×127 at 0x8761, 0x890A / 0x8AE4, 0x8B66 / 0x8CB5) but ALSO writes `inDungeon=1` @0x8030, which NWN never does, so the precedent is partial. §6a-ii's "reachable" column reproduces exactly (20/4/33/8/0; ECL0#1 coverage 4785/4808) ONLY under a walk that keeps BOTH `IF_*` successors live and does NOT narrow compare outcomes; the repo's checked-in `gen1_ecl_encounter_scan.successors()` narrows outcomes and yields 3/3/32/5/0 — that scanner limitation, not dialect, is the likelier cause of §6b's non-credible all-zero rows. `ECL5.DAX#51 @0x90FE` is unreached from the five header entries and unreferenced by any operand in the corpus, but decodes as coherent code (`SAVE #1,[0x7F12] / COMPARE [0x7F12],#1 / IF_NE / NEWECL #1 / GOSUB [0x810C]`) — dead/unreferenced code, not "string payload". Triboar/Floodblest/Nightsedge are identified only; their maps and routes were not walked. Test L honestly records that this route does NOT discriminate the dialect (ECL_GEN1 / ECL_GEN1_SHORT / ECL_GEN1_SHORT_GATEWAY give identical output on every service arm); the long-frame dialect is inherited from `neverwinter-nights-dos-eclinit.md`. A real engine defect is disclosed and not locked in by the golden: `EclVm.rvalue()` (vm.ts:818-821) treats operand code 0x02 as a memory read where retail `Opperation.GetCmdValue()` returns a 16-bit immediate. No DOSBox-X, no emulator, no native trace.

wilderness.citation: docs/engine/research/neverwinter-nights-dos-format-coverage.md § Wilderness leg: structurally-absent (2026-08-05). A proven negative carrying the same two independent pieces of evidence Secret's wilderness leg -- the only prior exemplar of this verdict -- was closed on. (1) Whole-corpus scanner zero from a scan that actually ran: `tools/map_gen1_area_mode_writes.py --profile neverwinter-nights-dos` reports 0 statically reachable `SAVE ...,0x4BE6` sites (Area1.inDungeon, Area1 offset 0x1CC -- the single binary host flag the retail engine flips between GameState.DungeonMap and GameState.WildernessMap, and the only binary-provable engine-mode split in the Gen1 corpus) across 6 ECL archives (ECL0/1/2/3/5/7.DAX) and 33 script blocks, matching that doc's own independent 33-block inventory, decoded with the correct long-frame GEN1_WORD_SETS dialect (NWN is not one of the four short-frame titles, so there is no dialect desync). CRITICAL: this zero was not obtainable before 2026-08-05 and the previous zero was a FALSE NEGATIVE -- neverwinter-nights-dos was missing from GEN1_PROFILE_IDS, so the profile was filtered out of build_report() before a single block was read, emitting `"games": []` while printing "gen1 area-mode writes: 0", which is indistinguishable from a real negative at the CLI. That is the same scope bug, in the same tuple, that was fixed for death-knights-of-krynn on 2026-07-18 and never generalized. Gateway is the control proving the repair yields true positives: it went 0 -> 24 and the repaired scanner independently rediscovered BOTH of Gateway's already-proven legs -- ECL6.DAX#21 SAVE 0 -> 0x4be6 at vaddr 0x808e (value 0 = WildernessMap, its proven wilderness leg) and ECL5.DAX#19 SAVE 1 (Sundabar, its proven town leg, correctly inDungeon=1). (2) NWN ships DUNGCOM.DAX + RANDCOM.DAX and NO WILDCOM.DAX, confirmed by direct file listing; measured the same way in the same run, Secret ships DUNGCOM.DAX only while Gateway, Treasures and Pools of Darkness all DO ship WILDCOM.DAX, so Secret's negative is demonstrably not being over-applied. The counter-argument is addressed rather than ignored: RANDCOM's outdoor-looking prop tiles do not imply a WildernessMap mode, because per ovr011.cs SetupGroundTiles() RANDCOM is always layered on top of whichever 24x24 bank is active -- an overlay, not the mode selector. Scope: this claims NWN's retail ECL contains no statically reachable overland/area-mode transition and no wilderness floor bank ships, bounded by static reachability from the five ECL header entry points -- the same bound every row in gen1-area-mode-writes.md carries. It does not claim NWN has no outdoor areas. Regenerated report: docs/engine/research/gen1-area-mode-writes.md (corpus total 128 -> 152). Tier unchanged at `persistent`; middle, ending, town and quest remain outstanding.

quest.citation: QUEST — PROVEN (cross-archive), with the setter-uniqueness claim narrowed. Kraken Society dock password, `[0x32C8]`/`[0x32CA]`. Doc: `docs/engine/research/nwn-quest-flag.md`. Test: `packages/engine/test/nwnQuestFlag.test.ts` (15 tests, all passing, not skipped; retail `D:\Games\Neverwinter Nights DOS\neverwinter-nights\neverwint\`). CROSS-ARCHIVE CORE (independently re-measured): over all 33 blocks of ECL0/1/2/3/5/7.DAX, `[0x32CA]` is the ONLY memory word in the entire game that has a writer somewhere and a reader block with no local writer — that block being `ECL1.DAX#14`, whose 25 `COMPARE [0x32ca],#n` arms (`@0x9461 = 03 01 ca 32 00 01` …) select a password word it never sets. SETTER — exactly one corpus-wide site writes the password-CONSOLE value (the clamped `INPUT_NUMBER` result held in `[0x7F79]`) into either cell, and it writes both: `ECL5.DAX#51` (5529 bytes), descriptor-37 console, `@0x9572 = 09 01 79 7f 01 c8 32` and `@0x9582 = 09 01 79 7f 01 ca 32`, bracketed by `@0x9579 = 09 00 0e 01 c5 4b` (SAVE #14->[0x4bc5]), `@0x957f = 38 00 11` (PROGRAM #17), `@0x9589 = 09 00 01 01 c5 4b`, `@0x958f = 38 00 11`. `[0x4BC5]` has exactly two operand references corpus-wide, both those writes, and is read nowhere in ECL; `38 00 11` gives 5 raw hits of which only these 2 are instruction starts (the 3 in `ECL2.DAX#26` are operand-byte coincidences). IT IS NOT THE ONLY WRITER OF THE CELLS — 37 reachable writes exist corpus-wide: 29 day-cache `SAVE [0x4bca]` writes (28 -> `[0x32C8]`, 1 -> `[0x32CA]` at `ECL1.DAX#17 @0x8caf`) plus `ECL1.DAX#16 @0x8af6 SAVE [0x4bc9],[0x32c8]` (the hour, 0-23), `ECL1.DAX#17 @0x8dad`/`@0x9153 SAVE #255,[0x32ca]`, `ECL2.DAX#26 @0x8cd0 SAVE #1,[0x32c8]`, `ECL2.DAX#27 @0x9336 SAVE #1,[0x32ca]` and `@0x933d SAVE #0,[0x32ca]`; four of those deposit values inside the 0-25 table range. `[0x32C8]`/`[0x32CA]` are therefore general-purpose per-area persistent slots of which the dock password is one use. CONSUMER A (CROSS-ARCHIVE) — `ECL1.DAX#14` (5668 bytes), descriptor 112 = `GEO1.DAX#14` cell (15,6): index = descriptor-104 = 8; ON_GOSUB pre-gate arm 8 = `0x843d` = `COMPARE #0,#1; RETURN` (always fires, no time or `[0x2AF8]` consumed-check); ON_GOTO body arm 8 = `0x8eed`: `PICTURE #94`, `LOAD_MONSTER #44,#2,#44`, `LOAD_MONSTER #94,#4,#94`, `COMBAT`, then `@0x8f92 = 02 01 56 94` (GOSUB the 26-entry ladder at 0x9456) and `@0x8f96 = 11 81 1e 7b` (PRINT the selected word) inside "TELL THE MAN AT THE DOCK IN NEVERWINTER, THE PASSWORD IS '<word>' FOR TRAVEL TO THE PURPLE ROCKS." Reachable in play: from `ECL1.DAX#12`'s trapdoor hand-off (`0x9d20/0x9d26/0x9d2c` = (11,6), NEWECL #14), (15,6) is 32 legal steps away inside an 81-cell component. CONSUMER B (HEADLINE GATE) — `ECL5.DAX#51` descriptor 36 = `GEO0.DAX#1` cells (1,11) and (1,13); `ECL0.DAX#1` search_location 38-arm `ON_GOTO @0x8284` arm 36 -> `@0x92b7 = 03 01 4d c0 00 03` (facing WEST, IF_NE EXIT) -> `NEWECL #51`, arm 37 -> `@0x92c2 = 20 00 33`. In the overlay: night gate `COMPARE [0x4bc9],#5 / IF_LT` and `COMPARE [0x4bc9],#20 / IF_GE` @0x8bcc, then `@0x8dcd = 10 00 08 81 00 7b` (INPUT_STRING #8), `@0x8dd3 = 02 01 52 93` (GOSUB the `[0x32c8]` ladder at 0x9352), `@0x8dd7 = 03 81 00 7b 81 1e 7b`, `@0x8dde = 16` (IF_EQ), `@0x8ddf = 01 01 7c 8e`, accept arm `@0x8e7c = 32 00 46` (FIND_ITEM #70) `@0x8e7f = 00` (EXIT); refusal arm prints the "SMALL PURPLE SQUID" brush-off, `PROGRAM #5`, `NEWECL #1`. Note that `[0x32C8]` is read and written inside `ECL5.DAX#51` itself, so the cross-ARCHIVE property is carried by the `[0x32CA]` side alone. THE TWO LADDERS were re-decoded from the retail 6-bit packed strings and are byte-order-identical 26-entry tables (FUTURE, TIME, FRONT, RIPE, STORM, JUNGLE, VISION, MATAGA, BORK, TWAIN, MOUNTAIN, WOODS, PALADIN, BARDICHE, GNOME, STATUE, GODDESS, UNDOMIEL, TEMPLE, RAPTURE, EMPIRE, VIOLIN, FIEND, PENDENT, OMINOUS, DUNGEON), differing only in the cell compared. END-TO-END, real EclVm, real bytes: the console writes both cells and the in-script re-display reads the new word back; that memory carried into `dialogueForCell(ECL1#14, 112)` yields the 44x2/94x4 combat then the note naming the same word; carried into the descriptor-36 gate the doorman EXITs on that word for all 26 indices. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: a different but real table word -> `chain` to block 1 with the PURPLE SQUID text, all 26 indices, plus empty/"XYZZY"/"PASSWORD"; facing north on (1,11) -> no chain; `[0x4bc9]=12` (day) -> the empty-dock description and chain to block 1, `INPUT_STRING` never reached. CAVEATS (all disclosed, none hidden): (i) the descriptor-37 console at `GEO0.DAX#1` (4,0) is provably WALK-UNREACHABLE — forward BFS from `ECL0#1`'s own byte-grounded spawn (8,7) covers 194 cells and excludes it, and a reverse BFS shows only {(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(4,0)} can ever step into it, disjoint from that component and containing none of the seven declared entry poses (7,0),(10,5),(15,7),(7,15),(2,6),(1,11),(8,7), all under the engine's permissive door rule (`explorer.ts:163`); the in-play source of the index is host/save-side and UNLOCATED. (ii) The per-area-bank reading of `SAVE #n,[0x4bc5]; PROGRAM #17` is an INFERENCE — NWN's `PROGRAM` dispatch in GAME.OVR was not disassembled — and the leg's "the note always names exactly the word the doorman expects, including at the untouched default 0 = FUTURE" holds ONLY under that reading. Under the alternative single-global-word reading neither cell is untouched by the time the party crosses from area 14 to area 1, and the two desync. The leg does not discriminate between the two readings; its supporting-but-not-conclusive evidence for per-area storage is the 28-block `COMPARE [0x4bca],[0x32c8]` / `SAVE [0x4bca],[0x32c8]` "already visited today" idiom, which only works if the slot is per-area, plus `ECL0.DAX#1` referencing `[0x32C8]` zero times. (iii) `FIND_ITEM #70`'s meaning is unresolved; "the doorman accepts" means only that the VM terminates `exited` and never emits the refusal text. (iv) Static CFG + GEO graph only; no DOSBox-X. (v) The `[0x4BC9]` = hour label is borrowed from this repo's CoK documentation (`docs/engine/research/cok-improvement-loop.md`), not re-derived from NWN's host; the leg needs only "some engine word forks day vs night", which the test asserts behaviourally. (vi) Reproducing the 93.6% corpus / 25.1% `ECL5#51` BFS coverage requires `scan_block`'s COMPARE-outcome reset, not `decode_one`/`header_entries`/`successors` alone (those three give 12.3% and never reach the console). ending.citation: RESOLVED 2026-08-07 (docs/engine/research/dqk-0032-writer.md; anchored in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts cases G and H). STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. The prior BLOCKED verdict rested on 'nothing in the 47-area ECL corpus ever writes [0x0032] nonzero'. That statement is TRUE and IRRELEVANT: [0x0032] is not a story flag. DQK.EXE's ECL operand resolver intercepts address 0x32 in a class-0 special-address table (25a4:0897, values at DQK.EXE file 0x040BB3) and dispatches it to 25a4:099c = a0 f3 c9 (mov al,[0xc9f3]) -- the wall type of the map edge the party faces, recomputed from the GEO planes by 2f0d:0628 on every move and every turn (all four writers of 0xC9F3 are that same recompute). The write path (25a4:06d2, table at file 0x0409E8) has NO entry for 0x32, so the four corpus SAVE #0,[0x0032] sites are dead stores against a byte the read path never consults. Independent cross-check that does not depend on any disassembly judgement: the same table maps ECL [0x002d] -> [0xc9f4], and 0x002d is the Gen2 cellDescAddr this project established years earlier from an unrelated direction, pinning the whole [0xc9f0..f4] X/Y/facing/wallType/cellDescriptor block (the same 5-tuple already located for DoK). THE ENDING DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT: area 66 dispatches on AND #0x7F,[0x002d]->[0x009B] at 0x8669 then ON_GOTO with 15 arms; arm 14 (0x9D18) is gated ONLY on the [0x00A0] step counter and issues GOSUB 0x9F03; NEWECL #67. ECL #67 is the finale (Takhisis on a burnished throne before the portal, golden bell) and is a cutscene, not a map -- its four non-init entries all point at one stub. Arm 14's cell is descriptor 0x8E at (27,4), the ONLY such cell, 38 steps from area 66's scripted landing pose (6,21) written at 0x80B1. Note the pose is written twice: 0x8055's (29,21) only stages the 17-frame 'FALLING BETWEEN WORLDS' loop and sits in a 110-cell region that CANNOT reach the ending; both are asserted in case H so the distinction cannot silently rot. Combined with the already byte-proven ingress chain area 5 -> 62 -> 64 -> 66 (docs/engine/research/dqk-ending-ingress.md), the ending is reachable by ordinary play. Side effect of this investigation: it exposed a real engine bug -- Gen2 GEO header order is (height, width), not (width, height), so 8 of the 20 DQK maps were being transposed; fixed in packages/engine/src/loaders/geo.ts + geoEncode.ts.

quest.citation: Investigated 2026-08-07 by a 5-finder + 5-adversarial-refuter workflow (docs/engine/research/dqk-campaign-legs.md); every claim below was then INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED FROM THE RETAIL BYTES BY THE OPERATOR and pinned in packages/engine/test/dqkCampaignLegs.test.ts before this status was written. Agent findings alone were not accepted as evidence. STATIC/BYTE-ONLY: no DOSBox-X, GameLink, emulator or screenshot evidence. QUEST = [0x0187] bit 0x20, written in area 55 and read in area 54. Case C: setter area 55 @0x80DD `30 01 87 01 00 20 01 87 01` OR [0x0187],#0x20 -> [0x0187]; reader area 54 @0x977F `2f 01 87 01 00 20 01 bf 00` AND [0x0187],#0x20 -> [0x00BF], then @0x9788 `03 01 bf 00 00 00 17` COMPARE [0x00BF],#0 / IF_NE. An ALIGNMENT-FREE census over all 47 areas (truncation-immune, so an opcode-table error cannot desync it) proves exactly TWO areas name [0x0187] at all: 54 and 55. IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION added during operator verification and NOT present in the finding: [0x0187] is a shared BITFIELD, not a single flag -- enumerating every OR-write of an immediate into it corpus-wide gives bits [0x01,0x04,0x08,0x10,0x20,0x40,0x40,0x40,0x80]. So 'sole setter of the WORD' would be FALSE; 'sole setter of the BIT' is what is true, and bit 0x20 is written exactly once, only by area 55 @0x80DD. Negative control on the clear side: area 54 @0x8B24 carries an AND clear-mask of 0xBF, which PRESERVES bit 0x20 (it clears 0x40), so nothing in the corpus ever clears this bit. DECLARED LIMIT: the census matches operands naming the address LITERALLY; opcode 0x35 SAVE_TABLE writes a COMPUTED base+offset and would be INVISIBLE to it -- the middle leg's own helper is exactly such a computed write. SCOPE NOTE: areas 54 and 55 are ADJACENT ids, unlike the Secret's-Sixth-Route precedent's non-adjacent blocks.
